title: Judges 21
paragraphs: ¹ Now the men of Israel had taken an oath at Mizpah: "None of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite." ² The people came to Bethel and sat before God until evening, wailing loudly. ³ "LORD, God of Israel," they cried, "why has this happened in Israel — that today one tribe is missing from Israel?" ⁴ The next morning the people rose early, built an altar there, and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. ⁵ Then the Israelites asked, "Which of the tribes of Israel did not come up with the assembly to the LORD?" They had bound themselves with a solemn oath that anyone who did not come up to Mizpah before the LORD would be put to death.

⁶ The Israelites grieved for their brother Benjamin. "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel," they said. ⁷ "How can we provide wives for those who are left, since we've sworn by the LORD not to give them our daughters?" ⁸ They asked, "Which of the Israelite tribes did not come to Mizpah before the LORD?" They found that no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the assembly camp. ⁹ When the people were counted, not a single person from Jabesh-gilead was there. ¹⁰ So the assembly sent twelve thousand warriors with orders: "Go and put the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead to the sword, including the women and children."

¹¹ "This is what you must do," they were told. "Kill every man and every woman who has slept with a man." ¹² They found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young women who had never slept with a man, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan. ¹³ The whole assembly sent a message to the Benjamites at the rock of Rimmon, offering them peace. ¹⁴ Benjamin returned at that time, and the Israelites gave them the women from Jabesh-gilead who had been spared — but there were not enough to go around. ¹⁵ The people felt sorry for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.

¹⁶ The elders of the assembly asked, "How can we find wives for those who are left, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed? ¹⁷ There must be survivors for Benjamin's descendants so that a tribe of Israel is not wiped out. ¹⁸ But we cannot give them our own daughters as wives, because the Israelites swore an oath: 'Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to a Benjamite.'" ¹⁹ Then they thought of something. "Look," they said, "there is an annual festival of the LORD at Shiloh — north of Bethel, east of the main road that runs from Bethel up to Shechem, and south of Lebonah." ²⁰ So they told the Benjamites, "Go and hide in the vineyards,

²¹ and watch. When the young women of Shiloh come out to join in the dancing, rush out from the vineyards and each of you seize a wife from among them and go to the land of Benjamin. ²² If their fathers or brothers come to us with a complaint, we'll tell them, 'Do us this favor, for we couldn't get wives for all of them in the war. You aren't guilty of breaking your oath, since you didn't give your daughters to them — they took them.'" ²³ The Benjamites did as they were told. Each man caught a wife from among the dancers. They went back to their own land, rebuilt the towns, and settled in them. ²⁴ The Israelites also left at that time, each returning to his own tribe and clan, and they all went back to their own lands. ²⁵ In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in their own eyes.
